questions.q: What is an index fund, per the passage?
options: A fund run by the stock exchange to beat the averages by trading
A fund that mirrors an index's holdings instead of picking stocks
A fund that picks the best stocks in order to outperform the market
A fund that holds only bonds and avoids stock-market exposure
questions.explain: It replicates an index's performance using passive management, not stock picking.

questions.q: What was the first open-end index mutual fund for retail investors?
options: First Index Investment Trust
Samsonite pension fund
Qualidex Fund
Dimensional Fund Advisors
questions.explain: The Qualidex Fund, started in 1970, tracked the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

questions.q: What nickname did competitors give Bogle's first fund?
options: Bogle's gamble
Bogle's folly
Un-American trust
The loser's fund
questions.explain: It was derided as 'un-American' and nicknamed 'Bogle's folly'.

options: Arbitrageurs trading ahead of known index rebalancing
Fund managers tipping off favored clients before trades
Index providers charging fees before new stocks are added
Funds buying a stock ahead of its addition to the index
questions.explain: Because index trades are announced in advance, algorithmic traders siphon value, which shows up as tracking error.

questions.q: Why did the Dow-based and equally weighted early funds struggle?
options: They were closed to all investors outside the institutions
They charged heavy sales loads that wiped out any gains
Regulators banned them after the 1973 market downturn
They were not market-cap weighted, making them costly or impractical
questions.explain: The passage says the price-weighted Dow needed costly rebalancing and the equal-weighted Samsonite fund proved impractical.
